Taking apart the VORSA aura edit: cuts, beats and sounds, measured

Source: vorsa_final.mp4 · 17.6 s · 1080x1920 · 30.00 fps · audio: yes

Measured, not watched or heard. Cuts come from frame differences, sound from band energy and onsets, words from a speech model. Claude cannot hear this file: every SFX class is a guess from the spectrogram's shape, and the beat tracker will invent a tempo for speech or a beatless pad (check pulse). Look at the sheets and the spectrogram before quoting a number.

Picture

  • Cuts: 35 hard, 32 jump. Hard = the picture is replaced. Jump = a sudden change in the same framing: a jump cut, or a graphic popping or swapping in one frame.
  • Average shot length: 0.49 s between hard cuts (median 0.40); 0.26 s counting jump cuts.
  • Cuts per minute: 228.4; cuts per beat 1.52

Dense sheets for Claude to read, 8 fps, 3 s each: sheets/s0000.0.jpg, sheets/s0003.0.jpg, sheets/s0006.0.jpg … (6 in all)

Zoom > 0 = push in; pan in % of the frame per second. A negative zoom done mostly in the first third reads as a zoom-settle (the shot lands zoomed in and eases out). Measured from 0.1 s after the cut, so the first frames of a settle are missing. Low tracked = flat graphics with few features: don't trust that row.

TAKE (transferable): fill by looking at the sheets

  • Average shot length and cuts per beat: 0.49 s between hard cuts (median 0.40 s, exactly one beat at 150 BPM), 0.26 s counting jump cuts. Long holds are rare and earned: 0.73 s on the first push-in, 1.47 s on the closing lume dial. Bursts of 33–70 ms cuts sit on the drop and on each freeze-stop.
  • How type enters and leaves: very little type, and only numbers or the name. A counter steps 06000 → 30000 → 36000 on the ticks, blown out and soft like a lens flare, not set on top; the name sits behind the glass in the dial, then is lit in lume as the lights go out. No captions, no lower thirds.
  • Camera language and transition logic: macro only, the subject never seen whole until 2.0 s. Every shot moves (ORB: +3 to +18 % push-ins, most of the zoom done in the first third, so shots land and settle). Transitions are hard cuts and same-framing jump cuts that read as stutters or freeze-stops; the drop flips to an inverted, lume-tinted impact frame.
  • Palette roles (ground, text, accent): black ground; steel and white for the subject; one saturated blue for the dial (held back until the drop: the first half is black and white); lume green as the only glowing accent; a single pink-red seconds hand as the pointer.
  • Texture and lighting: shallow depth of field with round bokeh, soft bloom and halation on highlights, light sweeping across the bezel, a crushed black floor, fine grain. Product-shoot lighting, not stylised graphics.
  • Sound feel (what the numbers above say, in words): a steady 150 BPM grid (pulse 1.02) with a 10 Hz tick layer: 78 of 106 transients are clicks, so the hi-hat is the movement itself. Low thuds land on the hard cuts. Two true silences in the spectrogram (5.9–6.4 s before the drop, ~12 s and ~14.3 s as freeze-stops) carry the structure: the drop is the restart after a stop. Mastered to −14.1 LUFS with a wide 9.9 LU range, because the silences are real.
  • Signature techniques (1-2, described abstractly): (1) make the subject's own mechanism the rhythm section: its tick rate is the tempo, its stop is the pre-drop silence, its restart is the drop. (2) Withhold colour and the hero angle until the drop, then give both at once.

LEAVE (recognisably theirs)

  • Shot order and compositions: the counter push-in on the seconds hand, the bezel orbit, the exploded caseback with the blue screw, and the lume dial close as the end frame.
  • Set pieces, script and copy, metaphors, logo moments: the hacking-seconds silence as the pre-drop stop, "36000" as the number on screen, and the name lit in lume at the end. These are this edit's own ideas; reuse the principle (the product's mechanism sets the edit's clock), not these moments.
